report.headline: No reliable root cause identified.

claims.text: The payment-svc database pool wait p95 ms metric shows a high value (371.27 ms) for 30 seconds, indicating potential database connection delays.
The payment-svc error rate metric shows zero errors over the entire incident window, indicating no service failures.
The payment-svc latency p50 ms metric shows a consistent value (50.63 ms) with no significant spikes, indicating normal request processing times.
The payment-svc latency p95 ms metric shows a high value (427.68 ms) with fluctuations, indicating potential database connection delays.
The checkout-svc logs show multiple timeout errors (2000ms) for payment calls, indicating that checkout-svc is timing out when trying to communicate with payment-svc.
The payment-svc deployment history shows multiple deployments of version 2.4.1 and 2.4.2, with the most recent deployment (d-766) being a manual restart of payment-svc 2.4.1.

unresolved_questions: Why did the payment-svc database pool wait p95 ms metric spike to 371.27 ms?
Why did the checkout-svc logs show multiple timeout errors for payment calls?
report.next_check: Check the database connection pool configuration for payment-svc to verify if there was a recent change that could have caused the wait time increase.

parsed.rationale: The evidence shows a deployment of payment-svc version 2.4.1 (commit b7ae74f) that reduced pool acquire timeout from 3s to 1s (per CHANGELOG). This directly correlates with the payment-svc db_pool_wait_p95_ms metric exceeding 200ms for 30 seconds. The checkout-svc logs show payment timeouts but are likely a symptom of the pool timeout change rather than the root cause. Payment-svc restarts are observed but are a consequence of the deployment change, not the root cause.
